root_cause.text: The use of cancel_delayed_work_sync() in tls_sw_cancel_work_tx() leaves a race window where a concurrent path (e.g., tls_write_space) can schedule the delayed work after cancellation, causing a use-after-free when the work handler runs on a freed TLS object.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description and commit message detail the exact race: CPU0 sets BIT_TX_SCHEDULED and calls cancel_delayed_work_sync, while CPU1 tests and sets the bit in tls_sw_write_space, then schedules the work after the cancel completes. The patch replaces cancel_delayed_work_sync with disable_delayed_work_sync to close this window.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix potential race condition by using disable_delayed_work_sync to prevent re-queueing of TLS TX work after cancellation during cleanup.
intent_record.what: Changed `cancel_delayed_work_sync` to `disable_delayed_work_sync` on `ctx->tx_work.work` in the function `tls_sw_cancel_work_tx`.
intent_record.how: The function now disables the delayed work instead of just canceling it, which prevents the work from being re-queued after the call, ensuring it remains disabled even if a rearm attempt occurs.
